root_profile.summary: Kökün dalları fiziksel örtme çekirdeğinden gece ve suyun örtücülüğüne, tohum ile bitki kılıflarına, dinî gerçeği veya nimeti reddetmeye ve günah yükünü gidermeye uzanan radyal bir yapı gösterir; ayrıca uzak yer, dağ geçidi, boyun eğme, taçlandırma ve aynı biçimli bitki-madde adları gibi sözlüksel olarak ayrışmış dallar bulunur.

text.arabic_uthmani: عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يَرْحَمَكُمْ ۚ وَإِنْ عُدتُّمْ عُدْنَا ۘ وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ حَصِيرًا

baseline.text: Rabbiniz belki size merhamet eder. Ama siz dönerseniz biz de döneriz. Cehennemi inkâr edenler için bir kuşatma yeri yaptık.

findings.text: Tekrarlanan dönüşe verilen karşılık, açık kalan merhamet imkânının ısrarlı ret sonucunda kişiyi kuşatan ve hareketini kapatan bir sınıra dönüşebileceğini gösterir.

activation_trace.role: Hope for an interrupted milk-flow to return gives the modal opening a restorative, not merely uncertain, texture.
Progressive repair, nurture, and completion make the Lord the administrator of renewed viability.
Tenderness issuing in benefit supplies the restorative pole of the conditional cycle.
Return after departure, repeated in both verbs, supplies the mirrored motion that can reopen either relation or consequence.

changed_reading.after: Mercy is a live re-entry within a reciprocal system: repair remains available, but the course that is resumed determines which answering return is reactivated.
changed_reading.before: A hopeful promise of mercy followed by a threat to punish again.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence from possibility through lordly mercy to the doubled return construction.
baseline_models.mechanism: A restorative opening is held inside a reciprocal loop: lordly repair and tender benefit remain possible after interruption, while a renewed human return activates a renewed answering return.

activation_trace.role: Near kinship makes mercy a repair of belonging and relation, not only remission of penalty.
The womb as a protected generative interior gives mercy a re-forming and life-bearing spatial role.
Nurture by stages turns protective holding into an active process of restoration.
A holding-place that imprisons supplies the inverse interior: containment without generative restoration.

changed_reading.after: The alternatives are two opposed interiors: restored belonging under nurture or a carceral holding that arrests further return.
changed_reading.before: Mercy is leniency, and Hell is the punishment that follows its refusal.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The movement from yarhamakum to the final hasira, read through the holding images within both roots.
baseline_models.mechanism: Mercy can be modeled as protective re-affiliation: kinship and womb images gather life into a sustaining interior, whereas the terminal enclosure gathers by detention. The ayah presents opposed modes of being held.

activation_trace.role: Causing something to occupy a condition makes the enclosure an enacted state rather than a merely named location.
Covering and concealment supply the human-side material operation that the final confinement answers.
A mat made by joining strands supplies the image of spaces closed through tight interweaving.
The prison or confining place converts the woven closure into an explicit terminal function.

changed_reading.after: Hell is a deliberately constituted confining medium: concealment culminates in a tightly joined condition that holds its coverers.
changed_reading.before: Hell is a generic punitive destination for disbelievers.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction jaalna jahannama lil-kafirina hasira.
baseline_models.mechanism: Deliberate constitution, covering, tight joining, and detention form a material-spatial sequence. Those characterized by covering are assigned a medium whose parts close together and whose function is to prevent exit.

activation_trace.role: Habit, training, and repeated engagement make the human return a practiced trajectory rather than a single relapse.
Renewal after an earlier beginning gives both sides of the clause iterative force.
Continuance and abiding make the Lord's governance stable across repeated human episodes.

changed_reading.after: The ayah exposes a repeatable habit-loop: mercy interrupts the course, but practiced return renews the corresponding divine encounter.
changed_reading.before: If the offense happens once more, punishment happens once more.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same root governs both protasis and response in wa-in udtum udna.
baseline_models.mechanism: Return can harden into habit and repeated practice. The clause therefore diagnoses more than a second isolated offense: it describes a recurrent course whose resumption also renews the encounter with its consequence.

activation_trace.role: Kinship gives the mercy offer a relational and intergenerational object.
Staged nurture supplies the repair process by which continuity can be rebuilt.
Good that remains and grows supplies a durable environment for restoration rather than a momentary reprieve.
Being carried within a line of descent makes preserved genealogy the concrete continuity at stake.
Recognition of benefit supplies grateful service as the repaired relation's responsive form.

changed_reading.after: The mercy offer can reopen sustained lineage and relation after rupture, enabling a carried community to become gratefully responsive again.
changed_reading.before: The mercy offer concerns release from the immediately preceding punishment.

context_deltas.mechanism: Stable growing good, a lineage carried through danger, and gratitude for received benefit turn mercy into continuity repair. The offered return is not only survival from a sentence; it can restore a damaged collective line to sustained, grateful service.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies durable blessing, carried descent, kinship, nurture, and gratitude; I infer that mercy repairs collective continuity and its responsive relation. A live alternative is that these cues describe preservation and gratitude without specifying an intergenerational mechanism for 17:8.
structural_cues: 17:1 places growing blessing around a destination reached through darkness.
17:3 identifies descendants of those carried through danger and closes with a grateful servant.

activation_trace.role: The same motion of returning after departure on both sides condenses the surrounding historical recurrence into one reciprocal clause.
A temporal occurrence that repeats marks the announced corruption as a structured recurrence.
Restoring something to its prior place supplies the reversible turn between defeat and renewed capacity.
A return repeated after an earlier occasion names the restored turn as recurrence rather than a fresh unrelated event.
Doing good supplies the positive input whose benefit the verse directs back to the acting selves.
The harm that makes one fare badly supplies the negative input that also returns upon its agents.
Entering an interior twice makes recurrence spatially concrete immediately before the focus clause.

changed_reading.after: We returned compresses a morally indexed feedback cycle: restoration remains possible, but renewed conduct travels back toward its agents through a renewed divine response.
changed_reading.before: We returned means that God simply repeated an earlier punishment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The marked repetitions before the focus ayah and the reflexive assignment of good and evil establish a feedback architecture. A course passes, is restored, and recurs; what the community does is already directed back toward itself, so the doubled return in 17:8 is reciprocal without being a merely arbitrary retaliation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated occasions, a restored turn, repeated entry, and reflexive benefit or harm; I infer that the divine return answers the trajectory the community resumes. The materially live alternative is a sovereign renewal of punishment whose timing is historical but whose mechanism is not self-feedback.
structural_cues: 17:5 and 17:7 pair an earlier and a later promised event, while 17:7 repeats entry by comparison with the first time.
17:7 directs both good and evil reflexively toward the acting selves.

activation_trace.role: Beneficent tenderness supplies the opening whose practical channel the following guidance specifies.
The possibility of returning makes changed direction, rather than static identity, the focus of the warning.
Gentle indication toward a path supplies the actionable means of leaving the destructive cycle.
Uprightness, balance, and straightness define the corrected trajectory's geometry.
Purposeful action turns indicated direction into an enacted course.
Repair opposed to corruption names the state produced by the corrected course.
Recompense for work supplies the answering return on the repaired trajectory.
A consequence already present and readied supplies the opposed endpoint without erasing the offered route away from it.

changed_reading.after: Mercy also arrives as a usable path of course correction: direction, upright action, and repair let the agent return differently before the prepared endpoint is reached.
changed_reading.before: Mercy is an unspecified favorable decision that may follow repentance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The mercy possibility is operationalized as a route out of recurrence. Gentle direction points to an upright course, intended action realizes repair, and recompense answers that work; the opposed painful outcome is already prepared. Mercy therefore includes navigable correction before judgment, not only pardon after failure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an offered mercy, path-direction, upright action, repair, recompense, and a prepared alternative; I infer that guidance is mercy's preventive mechanism inside the return cycle. A live alternative is that 17:9 only begins a new contrast and does not explicate the mercy of 17:8.
structural_cues: 17:9 immediately follows the focus ayah by specifying guidance, uprightness, work, repair, and reward.
17:10 places a prepared painful outcome in parallel for those who reject the other trajectory.

activation_trace.role: Nurture by successive stages supplies the governing tempo of the response.
Return after an interval permits recurrence to be paced rather than instantaneous.
Calling down a disliked event supplies the case in which a demand can mistake harm for desired good.
Haste and premature advancement identify the faulty human tempo that paced governance corrects.
Effacement of a visible trace supplies a phase of obscurity within the larger temporal system.
Counted time and recurrence at known intervals supply measured cadence to return.
Detailed differentiation prevents repeated events from being collapsed into an undiscerned reflex.

changed_reading.after: The answering return is a measured phase within lordly governance: delay can expose what the agents are actually asking for and leave room for a different return.
changed_reading.before: If you return, We return sounds like an immediate mirrored retaliation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Human urgency collapses good and harm into the same demand, while the night-day system alternates concealment and visibility, counts recurring time, and differentiates particulars. The Lord's return is therefore better modeled as paced administration with an interval for discernment, not as impulsive tit-for-tat.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies human haste, harmful demand, alternating signs, counted recurrence, and detailed distinction; I infer that the conditional response is administered across a diagnostic interval. The alternative is that these temporal cues concern ordinary calendrical knowledge and do not qualify the response in 17:8.
structural_cues: 17:11 contrasts the human call for harm with the call for good and attributes the confusion to haste.
17:12 makes alternating signs support the counting of years and reckoning, then closes with exhaustive differentiation.

activation_trace.role: Mirrored return supplies the motion by which a resumed course comes back into encounter with its agent.
The confining place supplies the final embodied condition into which the disclosed course resolves.
Affixing something through binding judgment makes the record inseparable from its bearer.
A written record laid open supplies the disclosure operation rather than a newly invented charge.
The self as the very entity concerned makes judgment reflexive and personally recognizable.
Counting and account supply the operation by which the opened record is evaluated.
A heavy carried load supplies individualized consequence and blocks transfer to another bearer.

changed_reading.after: The renewed divine response can also disclose and embody what has adhered to each agent; external sovereignty and self-returning account remain simultaneous readings.
changed_reading.before: God returns from outside to impose a repeated punishment on a group.

context_deltas.mechanism: Conduct adheres to the agent, is opened as a legible record, is reckoned by the self, and cannot be transferred as another's load. This revises the reciprocal clause from purely external retaliation into disclosure: the divine return can make the resumed human course present to and against its own bearer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adhesion, opening, self-account, and nontransferable load; I infer that We return includes making the agents' resumed course return as disclosed consequence. The live alternative is that the account explains individual final judgment while 17:8 remains an externally imposed historical response.
structural_cues: 17:13 attaches each person's outcome at the neck and presents an opened record.
17:14 makes the person read and reckon that record.
17:15 states that guidance and error fall reflexively and that no bearer transfers another's burden.

activation_trace.role: Causation into a state supplies the focus ayah's transformation from repeated course to terminal condition.
A place whose function is detention supplies the terminal state's spatial form.
The repeated causative construction confirms that Hell is assigned as a resulting condition for a pursued trajectory.
Direct encounter with fire supplies the enclosure's active bodily exposure.
Blame and defect supply the relational judgment accompanying the spatial endpoint.
Expulsion and distancing supply the outward motion that precedes being held apart.
Sitting and becoming fixed in a place supply the arrested posture of the endpoint.
Separation from one's supporting company supplies the isolating social condition of abandonment.

changed_reading.after: Hasira names an enacted endpoint that combines bodily exposure, relational expulsion, immobility, and isolation.
changed_reading.before: Hasira names the place where punishment occurs.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later repetition of making Hell for someone adds contact with fire, blame, and expulsion; the closing warning adds sitting fixed and abandonment. Together these cues turn the focus enclosure into the endpoint of a trajectory: one is driven out of sustaining relation and then arrested in an isolating posture.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated state-making, fire contact, expulsion, fixed sitting, and isolation; I infer a trajectory from chosen orientation to arrested enclosure. The alternative is that the later predicates list independent punishments rather than stages or dimensions of one mechanism.
structural_cues: 17:18 repeats the focus ayah's making-Hell construction for the seeker of the immediate and follows it with bodily and relational predicates.
17:22 links making another deity with a fixed, blamed, unsupported posture.

remaining_uncertainties: The reciprocal clause can still be read primarily as an external sovereign response rather than as feedback or self-disclosure.
The womb, milk, and carried-lineage mechanism may be materially illuminating while remaining too branch-distant for unqualified prose.
The woven-mat and prison branches of hasira may coexist as material and functional layers, but the packet does not force their merger.
The timing model depends on reading the night-day and reckoning sequence as qualifying the response in 17:8 rather than beginning an independent topic.
strongest_changes: The doubled return became a morally indexed feedback cycle rather than a bare threat of repeated retaliation.
Mercy became both restored relation and a practical route of course correction through guidance, action, and repair.
The later attached record and self-account revised divine return into disclosed, nontransferable consequence without canceling sovereign response.
Hasira became an enacted confining condition whose material, bodily, relational, and postural dimensions coexist.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah compresses opposed forms of return and opposed forms of holding. Nearby context unfolds that compression through carried continuity, repeated historical turns, paced signs, navigable guidance, attached account, and a later contrast between unbarred giving and enclosure. The lactational restoration image is the most branch-distant but also the most distinctive latent activation.

activation_trace.role: Hope for milk to resume after cessation supplies the outlier's explicit restoration image.
The womb as the place where life develops supplies the generative vessel for restored sustenance.
A benefit or kindness that comes back supplies a positive return alongside the clause's punitive possibility.
Milk drawn while the animal is settled supplies a nearby image of accessible nourishment.
Inner bearing and fruit supply the gestational phase of the sustaining process.
Fullness and abundant milk supply the visible outcome of restored provision.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, mercy is the hoped-for resumption of a severed sustaining flow: life can again be carried, nourished, and made fruitful.
changed_reading.before: Perhaps your Lord will show mercy means that leniency may resume.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it connects branch-distant milk, gestation, and womb images across several roots. It remains valid as a material analogy anchored in the focus possibility, mercy, and return construction and reinforced by nearby carrying and abundant-milk branches. Downstream prose should present it as an exploratory model of restored sustenance, not as a lexical replacement for mercy or a claim about literal lactation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The conjunction of asa, yarhamakum, and the doubled awd.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the receptive posture that fails to register what remains extended.
Prevention through surrounding confinement supplies the bounded condition contrasted with unbarred giving.
A connected increase that supports another supplies provision as continuing extension to both groups.
Handing something over supplies gift as an outward movement rather than a withheld reserve.
Prohibition and restriction, explicitly negated in context, supply the antithesis to the focus confinement.

changed_reading.after: Provision can remain extended and unbarred while covering culminates in a bounded condition; deprivation and enclosure are therefore not identical mechanisms.
changed_reading.before: Hellish confinement is simply the withdrawal of divine provision.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading is surprising because it contrasts the focus enclosure with the later denial that lordly giving is barred, using related but nonidentical confinement images. It remains anchored in hasira and in the explicit extension, giving, and non-prohibition of 17:20. Downstream prose should frame it as a contrastive activation, not equate the roots or assert that punishment is wholly self-produced.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The confinement of the coverers at the ayah's close.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Return is answered by an enclosing return.** Doubled `ع و د:B001/B004` gives return and repeated habit; `ح ص ر:B004/B008/B012` supplies surrounding confinement, mat, and prison; `ك ف ر:B001/B004` covers truth or favor. The balanced *if you return, We return* is followed by an enclosure for those who cover over. I infer repeated refusal progressively weaves its own confining surface. Hell reads as the spatial completion of a habit, while mercy remains a live alternative before the loop closes.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:97's repeatedly rekindled fire sharpened `ح ص ر` here: enclosure is not passive containment but a maintained consequence answering recurrent return.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Recurrence terminates in enclosure.** Lexical evidence: `ح ص ر B004` (confinement, prevention, and surrounding) in `حَصِيرًا`, set against `ر ح م B001` (mercy and tenderness) in `يَرْحَمَكُمْ`. Structural cue: the mirrored `عُدتُّمْ عُدْنَا` closes 17:4–7's repeated cycle; 17:13, still in the focus window, binds each person's record to the neck. Assigned role: mercy leaves return open, whereas `حصر` closes movement when return hardens into repetition. Abductive move: the packet supplies recurrence and confinement; I infer that persistent recurrence causes the open cycle to become a closed boundary. Reading change: `حَصِيرًا` reads spatially as the final enclosure of repeated refusal, sharpening the contrast with offered mercy.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:13's neck-bound record sharpened the spatial force of `ح ص ر B004`; repeated refusal ends not just in punishment but in a closure that fixes the person inside consequence.

words.gloss_range: modal hope or near possibility, locally governing a mercy complement without making mercy an owned or already completed outcome
words.prose: {{ar:عَسَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿasā}}) opens the ayah with mercy as near possibility rather than possession. Its frozen verbal form still governs the following complement, so the first beat is grammatically active but modal: mercy is opened before the ayah tightens into condition and settled consequence. Its long opening vowel lets the hope word take audible space before the clipped return pair later in the ayah. The same hope-under-Lordship formula recurs in Surah 17 (17:79), while the boundary from 17:7 makes this opening feel like devastation decompressing into possible mercy.
words.root_gloss_range: hope, expectation, and nearness to realization; in divine speech the certainty-versus-possibility debate remains locally qualified by the surface hope form

topics.headline: frozen hope verb governs mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the opening word is not a loose adverb of optimism but a frozen verb that governs the mercy clause.
topics.reason: The local syntax identifies a hope construction headed by the word and completed by the governed complement.

topics.headline: near mercy without owned certainty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels mercy opened as desirable and near while the wording still withholds possession of the outcome from the addressees.
topics.reason: The divine-subject debate is preserved as pressure, but the local surface still uses the hope form and does not turn the first beat into a flat indicative assertion.

topics.headline: hope opening before conditional warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's movement from possible mercy to conditional return and then to settled assignment, with a same-surah hope-under-Lordship echo (17:79).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows tie the modal opener to the ayah's three-beat structure and to concrete same-surah recurrence.

topics.headline: long opening pace before clipped return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the hopeful opening take more recitational space before the later return pair contracts into terse reciprocity.
topics.reason: The orthographic and phonetic rows add a distinct pacing payoff that supports, rather than replaces, the modal reading.

words.gloss_range: the addressees' own governing and nurturing Lord, explicit as subject of the hope construction
words.prose: {{ar:رَبُّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbukum}}) makes the possible mercy relational: it comes from the addressees' own Lord, not from an abstract source. The singular governing title carries a plural suffix, compressing one Lordship relation over the whole addressed community; that same collective is then mercy's object and the condition's human agent. The relation can hold mercy and warning together, since the same surah repeatedly uses Lordship language for governance, mercy, and consequence (17:24, 17:39, 17:54).
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, mastery, sustaining, nurturing, and bringing to completion; locally the possessive relation makes authority and restorative care converge

topics.headline: possessive title binds Lord to addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that possible mercy is framed through an already established Lord-addressee relation.
topics.reason: The noun is construct-like with a bound plural possessive suffix, making the addressee relation part of the surface form.

topics.headline: explicit subject bears mercy possibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the Lord, not the addressees, grammatically bears the hope construction's possible mercy.
topics.reason: The local attachment evidence marks this word as the subject of the opening hope verb.

topics.headline: one plural addressee crosses the clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same collective addressee from possible mercy into the later condition and warning.
topics.reason: The plural suffix is repeated across the mercy and return clauses, preserving one addressed community.

topics.headline: authority carries restorative care
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears Lordship as governing authority with nurture and staged restoration, not as bare sovereignty alone.
topics.reason: The root range supports nurture and completion pressure, while the local title remains the selected Lordship noun.

topics.headline: Lordship links mercy and consequence fields
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this title joining the surah's repeated governance vocabulary, including mercy formulas and warning nodes (17:24, 17:39, 17:54).
topics.reason: The cited same-surah references support a local Lordship field without making every branch active in this word.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive complement particle that turns the mercy action into the governed content of hope
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) is the hinge that makes mercy the content of the opening hope construction. It governs the following verb's mood, so the mercy clause is not an independent factual assertion. The standalone particle also leaves the dependency visible: hope and mercy are joined through grammar rather than simply placed side by side.

topics.headline: particle governs the mercy verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is grammatically held in potential mood under the hope construction.
topics.reason: The local grammar marks the particle as introducing the governed complement and placing the following verb in subjunctive mood.

topics.headline: complement use selected locally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads the mercy clause as the content of hope, not as a separate purpose, result, or explanation clause.
topics.reason: The broader particle range is narrowed by its position after the hope verb and before the governed mercy verb.

topics.headline: standalone hinge between hope and mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can see a small separate word carrying the link between modal hope and mercy content.
topics.reason: The word is an independent particle in the surface sequence and supplies the syntactic bridge.

words.gloss_range: direct divine mercy toward the addressed group, locally subjunctive under the hope construction and expressed as simple Form I action
words.prose: {{ar:يَرْحَمَكُمْ}} ({{tr:yarḥamakum}}) gives the opening hope its content, but its mood keeps mercy potential rather than already declared. The attached plural object makes the addressees the direct recipients of mercy, while the Form I verb presents simple directed compassion. The repeated plural suffix binds the Lordship title to this mercy verb by sound as well as grammar. The root's protection and tenderness field remains meaningful, and the same mercy vocabulary threads through Surah 17, including the later contrast between hope here and divine will in 17:54.
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, tenderness, beneficent inclination, and protective encompassing; locally directed as action upon the addressees rather than intensified or reflexive derivation

topics.headline: mercy remains inside the hope frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that mercy is the hoped-for content, not an already completed declaration.
topics.reason: The verb is governed by the preceding particle in the hope construction.

topics.headline: the addressees receive mercy directly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressed group is not merely near mercy but grammatically receives it as the verb's object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the bound plural suffix as the verb's direct object.

topics.headline: tender protection colors the action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels mercy as protective and tender beneficence, while the local verb still selects direct mercy action.
topics.reason: The root-family image survives as semantic pressure without replacing the local Form I verb.

topics.headline: simple Form I rather than intensified stems
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the mercy presented as direct action, not as an intensified, reflexive, or invocation-shaped form.
topics.reason: The local form is Form I imperfect, so other derived-family values are contrastive rather than locally selected.

topics.headline: mercy thread across Surah 17
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this mercy verb as the first local opening of a same-surah mercy thread, with a pointed modality contrast at 17:54.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete same-surah recurrence and a boundary contrast that do not override the local grammar.

topics.headline: suffix sound binds Lordship and mercy

words.gloss_range: contrastive connective pivot from possible mercy into the conditional warning
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is small but it turns the ayah. It keeps the mercy clause connected while pivoting into a counter-scenario: possible mercy stands beside warning, not apart from it. Because the next word opens a condition, the connective reads as coordination charged with contrast.

topics.headline: mercy turns into warning condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah pivot from possible mercy to warning without severing the two clauses.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the conditional counter-scenario and therefore carries both connection and contrast.

topics.headline: mercy and warning are juxtaposed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's two emotional poles placed directly beside each other.
topics.reason: The row family captures a discourse payoff created by the local clause boundary.

topics.headline: single-letter connector bears transition load
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how little surface material is used to shift the ayah from hope to warning.
topics.reason: The formal note has a distinct payoff because the one-letter connector carries the clause transition.

words.gloss_range: open conditional particle that scopes over the human return and the divine answer, leaving relapse possible rather than presumed
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) keeps the warning open: it says if, not when. That matters because the ayah does not grammatically presume the addressees' return to wrongdoing, even as it makes the consequence ready. The particle also scopes over both terse return verbs, making the center of the ayah a compressed if-then rule. After the closed consequence chain of 17:7, this particle reopens the future as conditional logic.

topics.headline: if rather than when
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reversion remains morally possible rather than grammatically forecast as inevitable.
topics.reason: The local particle is the open conditional rather than an expected-time particle.

topics.headline: one particle governs the if-then pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two return verbs as one conditional relation, not two unrelated statements.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the protasis and apodosis under the conditional construction.

topics.headline: clipped center with omitted complements
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the warning land tersely as return-for-return, with both return targets left compressed.
topics.reason: The two following verbs are both absolute in the local frame, so supplied complements remain translation support rather than explicit Arabic wording.

topics.headline: closed consequence reopens as conditional logic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior closed causal arc reappear as a new future-facing conditional rule after 17:7.
topics.reason: The boundary row gives a concrete discourse transition into a new if-then structure.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural return or relapse in an open condition; locally not counting despite the bundle's root-tag noise
words.prose: {{ar:عُدتُّمْ}} ({{tr:ʿudtum}}) names the human side of the condition as return or relapse. Although perfect in form, it works under the open conditional as future-facing warning. The second-person plural ending makes the addressed group responsible for the protasis, and the absent complement keeps the relapse compressed: the wording does not spell out the target, but context supplies return to wrongdoing. The root-tag noise is narrowed away from counting; the payoff is cyclical reversion.
review_notes: The aligned root tag is retained in metadata, but the lexical prose follows the CRITICAL rows that identify the local word as return or reversion rather than counting.
words.root_gloss_range: the aligned tag points to counting or preparing, but the local word and CRITICAL evidence select return and recurrence pressure; counting is not active here

topics.headline: perfect form becomes future warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the perfect verb as a conditional future warning, not a report of a completed past return.
topics.reason: The verb stands after the open conditional particle, giving the perfect form hypothetical force.

words.gloss_range: first-person divine return or resumption in the answer to the condition, with the punitive complement left compressed
words.prose: {{ar:عُدْنَا}} ({{tr:ʿudnā}}) answers the human return with divine return. The subject is inside the verb, so the warning stays compact while direct divine agency enters the sequence. Its omitted complement is punitive response, not physical motion, and its matching perfect form makes the answer feel formally immediate: if the addressees return, the divine response returns. The two narrated cycles of corruption and punishment in 17:4-7 are thereby generalized into a repeatable conditional rule.

words.gloss_range: completed divine assignment or rendering, locally taking the named destination and its confining role as a double-object frame
words.prose: {{ar:جَعَلْنَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnā}}) closes the ayah with completed divine assignment. Its double-object frame does not merely mention the named destination; it renders that destination as a confining role for the designated class. The repeated opening sound between this verb and the following named object couples the act and assigned object audibly. The verb's root range is narrowed to assignment rather than creation, and its recurrence in Surah 17 makes the final clause part of a local refrain of divine configuring and warning (17:2, 17:6, 17:12, 17:18, 17:39).

words.gloss_range: the named eschatological destination as first object of the assignment verb, fixed as a proper foreign diptote rather than an indefinite punishment noun
words.prose: {{ar:جَهَنَّمَ}} ({{tr:jahannama}}) is the first object of the assignment frame, and the next descriptor tells what it is made to be. As a proper foreign diptote, it names a fixed destination rather than a generic punishment item. The etymological tension around the name can thicken the image with topographic and abyssal pressure, but the local payoff is the named place/state being assigned a confining role. A close parallel at 18:102 keeps the same named-destination-plus-recipient pattern but changes the descriptor, making 17:8's confinement word distinctive.

words.gloss_range: allocated to the definite plural agent-class of deniers or coverers, with the prefixed allocation particle marking designation rather than a direct object
words.prose: {{ar:لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:lil-kāfirīna}}) fuses allocation with a definite recipient class. The prefixed allocation particle makes the class designated recipients of the confinement, not the direct object of the making verb. The active participle keeps the label agentive: they are named by ongoing covering or denial, with ingratitude also in the root field. The final phrase widens the addressed history into a universal class tail, and the adjacent confinement word turns covering back upon the coverers.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative confinement descriptor, locally functioning as the named destination's assigned role or state for the deniers
words.prose: {{ar:حَصِيرًا}} ({{tr:ḥaṣīrā}}) is the ayah's final word and the role assigned to the named destination. Its local force is confinement: prison, enclosure, siege pressure, and even mat-like flooring gather into an image of a space that holds its recipients down and in. The accusative nunation leaves the descriptor indefinite and weighty at closure. Against the prepared-for-deniers formula of 2:24, this wording stresses assigned confining function. The rare form also answers the spatial violation of 17:7 with inescapable confinement and echoes same-root constriction later in 17:29.
